title: Benny Payne's joining date, from a phone call
summary: They phone Payne, who recalls joining on November 21, 1931 at the Audubon when billing became Cab Calloway and His Orchestra.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Now, when did Bennie Payne get in there, into Cab Calloway's band.
I don't know. He took Prince's place.
Why don't we call him up and ask him.
Thomas (3) - 26
Yeah, he took Prince's place. And we liked Bennie, because...
[PAUSE]
We just got through talking to Bennie Payne. We asked him about when he joined...
He said he joined the band in 1931, November the 21st, and we was playing the Audubon Theatre.
This is February 13, 1981. And Bennie has had a little stroke on his right side, but he says he's in the hospital now in California, and he's doing great. So he's supposed to be out in two weeks.
Oh good.
He said he's walking a little bit, and I'm so happy to hear that. And he talked to us. So what did he tell you, Foots?
He was telling me about salt. You know, that's what they harp on. Because they think that salt has a lot to do with your bloodstream.
What did he say about the band, the Missourians?
Well, he didn't say much about the Missourians...
Well, where did he join the band, Foots?
Thomas (3) - 27
He joined the band November 21, 1931. And he said that's the first date that the band played where its name had been changed to Cab Calloway and His Orchestra, Cotton Club Orchestra.
And it was at the Audubon Ballroom.
No, the Audubon Theatre.
Well, I don't know where the Audubon Theatre is, but the Audubon Ballroom I know. Was it the Audubon Theatre?
Yeah, it was the Audubon Theatre.
All right, so he came in. We noted that Cab and Bennie had been playing somewhere.
From the Blackbird show, yeah.
I guess it was. And Cab and Bennie struck a friendship over there, said that whichever one of them made it was going to look out for the other one.
Oh yeah? I guess so, yeah.
They made sort of a pact. That was his first ...(?)...
